steps.text: A card just dropped from the notch asking for your mic. Click Allow — that's the ear that hears you when you hold a key and talk.
steps.hint: If the system window doesn't appear, the card opens System Settings — flip the Switchboard toggle on.

steps.text: Next card: Accessibility. Drag the Switchboard chip into the list (or hit Open) and switch it on — this is the hand that points, clicks and types for you.
steps.hint: macOS has no one-click grant here, so you add Switchboard to the list yourself. The card waits.

steps.text: Last one: Screen Recording. Click Allow so I can glance at what's on your screen and actually help with it.
steps.hint: Grant it and the permission cards are done — the notch orb goes quiet. Press → to keep going.

steps.text: Now tap Control twice — ⌃⌃. The orb wakes, listens, and you can just say what you need. Try it, then press → .
steps.hint: This is your summon. Anytime, anywhere — ⌃⌃ and start talking.

steps.text: Put your cursor in any text field, then hold ⌃⌥ and speak. Let go and your words land right where the cursor is. Press → when you've watched it type.
steps.hint: Hold to talk, release to drop the text. No send button, no window — just your voice into the page.

steps.text: Last trick: double-tap Option — ⌥⌥ — to throw open the launcher. Every app and tool, one keystroke away. Give it a tap, then press → to finish.
steps.hint: ⌃⌃ to ask · ⌃⌥ to dictate · ⌥⌥ to launch. That's the whole keyboard. You're set.
